newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal up 13.2 pct from year ago -- AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal up 13.2 pct from year ago -- AAR.

text.p: U.S. intermodal rail freight rose 13.2 percent in the week ended March 22 from the year-ago week, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
AAR said intermodal traffic in the week totaled 170,442 trailers and containers compared with 150,587 a year ago. Intermodal does not include carloads.
Carloads in the March 22 week were 347,110, up 2.6 percent from 338,224 in the year-ago week.
Ton-miles rose 4.1 percent to 27.9 billion from 26.8 billion last year. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, equates one ton of freight hauled one mile.

AAR said the increase in rail traffic was led by sharp increases in motor vehicle loadings, which soared 44.4 percent to 22,787 loadings from 15,778 in the same period last year. AAR said this increase in motor vehicle loadings is related to last year's General Motors strike.

"Most of the increase this week can be attributed to the fact that the comparison week from last year saw the beginning of a strike against General Motors," AAR senior assistant vice president Craig Rockey said. Loadings of farm products
other than grain also increased 24.1 percent in the week to 1,374 carloads from 1,107 last year.
Compared to the year-ago week, grain mill products rose 8.8 percent to 10,266 carloads from 9,432, AAR said.
Sharp declines were reported in metallic ores, which fell 31.3 percent to 11,999 from 17,464 a year ago, and in carloads of coke, which decreased 9.2 percent to 5,256 carloads from 5,787.
In the first 12 weeks of 1997, AAR said carloads increased 3.6 percent from the same period last year. Ton-miles were up 4.3 percent and intermodal traffic rose 5.4 percent from the same 1996 period.

AAR also said carloads on Canada's two transcontinental railroads totaled 56,337 in the March 22 week, a 9.3 percent gain from a year ago, while intermodal traffic rose 5.3 percent to 25,692 trailers and containers from the same 1996 week.
